Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

otherwise adverb

or else, if not

also or else, else (if not), if not

classical

Cic. Off. 2.42: neque enim aliter esset jūs (Lewis & Short)
Nep. Them. 7 fin. (Lewis & Short)

aliter

adverb; the verb in the mood of the condition it stands for

otherwise, else

“If not, …”: aliter stands for a condition, so after an unreal one the verb is subjunctive (aliter esset, otherwise it would be). Its first sense is “in another way” (aliter atque, otherwise than).

Other words

  • sīn aliter (sīn minus) — but if not, otherwise

    conjunction and adverb, opening a clause · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 1.2.1: sīn aliter acciderit, hūmāniter ferēmus

    Where the “otherwise” is a whole condition: see if not.

  • aliōquī (aliōquīn) — otherwise, else; in other respects

    adverb, first in its clause · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 8.8.1: sī nōndum (et putō nōndum: aliōquī narrāssēs mihi) (Lewis & Short)

    From Livy on, and frequent in Pliny’s letters and Quintilian; not in Cicero (Lewis & Short). Lewis & Short notes that the form aliōquīn is doubted in the manuscripts.

Examples

  • jūs enim semper est quaesītum aequābile; neque enim aliter esset jūs

    for what was always sought was fair and equal law; otherwise it would not be lawCic. Off. 2.42 (Lewis & Short)

  • sīn aliter acciderit, hūmāniter ferēmus

    but if it turns out otherwise, we shall bear it like reasonable peopleCic. Att. 1.2.1

  • sī nōndum (et putō nōndum: aliōquī narrāssēs mihi)

    if you haven’t yet (and I think you haven’t, otherwise you would have told me)Plin. Ep. 8.8.1 (Lewis & Short)

See also if not, else, or.

SourcesLewis & Short: aliter · Lewis & Short: sin · Lewis & Short: alioqui
